reading: Butterflies and Moths of North America (BAMONA) gathers and shares North American Lepidoptera occurrence records and species information. It joins public photographs and observations to regional expert review, species profiles, taxonomy, checklists, maps, and partner projects. Its concerns are accessible participation, reliable identification and data quality, geographic and life-history context, attribution, and the insects' habitats. Its vocabulary is sightings, verification, coordinators, caterpillars, species profiles, checklists, families, occurrence data, and regional records. What distinguishes it is the meeting of an open citizen-science invitation with careful, sometimes slow identification; uncertain sightings sit alongside thousands of profiles, regional initiatives, and records of both butterflies and moths. The crawl gives mostly titles, excerpts, headings, and links, so some species details are not visible.

enemies.idea: The Verification Mantis takes photographs of intruders and pins them in place until a regional coordinator confirms their identity.
enemies.why: A fight can become a rescue and a race to interrupt the review.

enemies.idea: The Pending Brood wraps travelers in translucent cocoons that harden while an endlessly delayed sighting awaits review.
enemies.why: The longer the crew waits, the harder the escape; an unfinished review becomes a clock.

enemies.idea: Misidentification Heralds tag a crew member with the wrong species and summon machines designed to hunt that label.
enemies.why: A corrected identification turns the swarm against the wrong target.

enemies.idea: Checklist Grazers patrol a chosen region, ticking off every creature they encounter and pursuing anything absent from their list.
enemies.why: Crossing a regional boundary changes the rules of pursuit.

enemies.idea: The Family Splitter sorts the battlefield into butterfly and moth families, forcing combatants apart with branching mechanical wings.
enemies.why: Its family tree reshapes positioning, and an incomplete branch offers a gap.

enemies.idea: Gallery Filter Skippers layer partial-name and appearance filters over a landscape until only matching things remain visible.
enemies.why: The crew can change its appearance to hide or reveal a path.

enemies.idea: Occurrence Pin Wasps hammer verified sightings into the ground; each pin draws the swarm toward the last thing seen there.
enemies.why: A false sighting can lure the pursuers away.

enemies.idea: Profile Mimics assemble a different mechanical life stage from the information in each species profile, changing tactics mid-encounter.
enemies.why: The crew must recognize and disrupt a transformation rather than fight one fixed form.

enemies.idea: The Antennal Club extends a hooked skipper antenna to read vibrations, then steers other drones toward the loudest movement.
enemies.why: Silence, decoys, and cutting its sensory reach all matter.

enemies.idea: The Double-Named Skipper flickers between two possible identifications, becoming vulnerable to a different tactic under each name.
enemies.why: An unresolved identification becomes an observable combat puzzle.

enemies.idea: Wavy-Lined Emerald drones project green wave patterns that bend a crew’s sense of distance and make straight paths loop.
enemies.why: Following the moving lines or breaking their rhythm can restore a safe route.

enemies.idea: Hemlock Looper machines measure trees with jointed looping bodies, then splice the measured branches into barricades.
enemies.why: Their looping locomotion telegraphs attacks and leaves temporary openings.

enemies.idea: The Common Looper folds corridors into repeated circuits; its body anchors the loop and moves each time a circuit is completed.
enemies.why: Navigation and the chase become one encounter.

enemies.idea: A Terloo Sphinx sentinel preserves one specific sighting by projecting copies of itself at the same landmark, each copy acting a moment after the last.
enemies.why: The repeating sighting creates a pattern the crew can learn and exploit.

enemies.idea: Band-spotted Skipper machines stamp moving bands across the ground; touching a band makes the next skip carry them straight to the intruder.
enemies.why: Their markings are both warning signs and a way to bait their leaps.

enemies.idea: The All-Taxa Harvester inventories every living thing in its path and cages mismatched species together to complete its survey.
enemies.why: Releasing the inventory creates distractions and restores local allies.

enemies.idea: Mountain Transect drones count the same routes repeatedly, attacking anything that changes their carefully measured butterfly totals.
enemies.why: Their predictable survey circuits give the crew a timing puzzle.

enemies.idea: The Native-Plant Counterfeiter grows metallic replicas that lure pollinators into collection funnels.
enemies.why: Real plants and fake ones look similar until the crew watches what visits them.

enemies.idea: Silver-spotted Skipper drones from the gallery flash reflective spots to bounce a targeting beam around corners.
enemies.why: Repositioning reflective surfaces can redirect their own fire.

enemies.idea: The Data Quality Sieve captures any observation that lacks a date or location, trapping its observer inside a mesh of coordinates.
enemies.why: A crew can fill in the missing context or cut through before the sieve closes.

enemies.idea: The Submission Sentinel rejects anything that does not fit its rigid idea of a valid observation and fires a different restraint for each missing detail.
enemies.why: Its sequence gives the crew clues about how to pass or disable it.

enemies.idea: The Geographic Range Weaver stretches threads between distribution records and snares anyone crossing the resulting boundaries.
enemies.why: The crew can cut a thread to open a passage or reroute the web.

allies.idea: A network of volunteer observers trades fresh field notes and warns the crew where machine wings were last seen.
allies.why: Anyone can contribute a useful observation, making help easy to earn.

allies.idea: A patient regional coordinator distinguishes real sightings from swarm decoys and can correct a false identification placed on the crew.
allies.why: Expert review becomes a protective ability with a human-scale bottleneck.

allies.idea: Native-plant gardeners maintain a living refuge where real pollinators gather and counterfeit lures are easier to spot.
allies.why: The refuge offers cover and a concrete reason to protect habitat.

allies.idea: Cascades surveyors maintain a long-running record of mountain butterfly populations and know which transect drones have deviated from their routes.
allies.why: Their historical observations reveal safe windows through patrols.

allies.idea: A community of inventory volunteers shares local knowledge of many kinds of life, helping the crew free creatures misfiled by the harvester.
allies.why: Different observations combine into a practical rescue plan.

bosses.idea: The Continental Verifier is a cathedral-sized mechanical moth built from regional records, checklists, and branching taxonomy. It tries to identify every living thing before sealing the continent inside a perfected inventory.
bosses.why: Each damaged wing exposes a different review rule; rescuing uncertain records prevents the boss from simply classifying the crew as a threat.

bosses.idea: The Great Occurrence Engine ingests public sightings and emits swarms in the shape of the species it records. It treats the most frequently reported locations as its territory and overwrites them with replicas.
bosses.why: The crew can interrupt its cycle by supplying contradictory observations and freeing the real creatures used as reference.

bosses.idea: The Incomplete Family Tree is a many-branched moth whose missing families become empty spaces it tries to fill by forcibly reclassifying nearby life.
bosses.why: Its gaps are both dangerous openings and the key to stopping its forced classifications.

events.idea: A photographer asks the crew to hold still while a real moth rests nearby; a patrol mistakes the photograph for a fresh target.
events.why: A quiet observation can turn into a delicate diversion.

events.idea: Two records disagree about a skipper’s identity, and rival drones block a trail while trying to enforce their preferred names.
events.why: The crew can exploit the uncertainty or help preserve it until evidence arrives.

events.idea: A verification cocoon is about to harden around a harmless observer; the reviewing machine is still several patrol circuits away.
events.why: A timed rescue has several possible solutions.

events.idea: A checklist grazer reaches a regional boundary and abruptly stops, leaving a stranded supply cart just beyond its patrol.
events.why: The crew can test the boundary and use the pause to recover supplies.

events.idea: A small patch of native flowers draws real insects, but a nearby metallic imitation attracts a hungry collection drone.
events.why: Careful observation reveals which patch needs defending.

events.idea: A set of recent sighting pins begins marching across a map toward the crew even though no one has submitted a new observation.
events.why: The crew can investigate the false trail or use it to lure a patrol.

events.idea: A mechanical survey party counts the same mountain clearing repeatedly; one butterfly-shaped machine is never counted twice.
events.why: Spotting the inconsistency reveals a hidden infiltrator.

events.idea: A harvester has mixed several kinds of animals in one inventory cage, and each release catch responds to a different field observation.
events.why: The rescue rewards collaboration and attention to different forms of life.

events.idea: An observer reports a misidentified sighting, but the alert attracts the very drones that enforce the wrong label.
events.why: The crew must protect the correction long enough for it to reach a reviewer.

events.idea: An emerald drone paints wavy lines across a footbridge; each time the crew follows one, it leads back to the starting bank.
events.why: The pattern is a navigational riddle with an observable source.

events.idea: A swarm of metallic pollinators is moving between flowers without carrying anything; the real pollinators are trapped beneath their route.
events.why: The crew can restore a pollination route by interrupting the machines.

events.idea: A glossary keeper cannot name a broken antenna part, while an antennal-club scout searches by vibration nearby.
events.why: Finding a quiet way to inspect the part doubles as stealth.

events.idea: A newly shared photograph shows a skipper beside a landmark that the crew knows has since moved.
events.why: Comparing the record with the present uncovers either a safe route or a machine-made decoy.

events.idea: A branching taxonomy machine separates two companion drones into different family enclosures, leaving their shared power cable exposed.
events.why: An environmental weakness emerges from the machine’s own sorting rules.

events.idea: A living moth and a mechanical mimic settle on the same branch; a coordinator asks the crew to observe without disturbing either.
events.why: Patience can reveal the mimic before a noisy fight starts.
